text:
sam: Quick heads-up — I'm planning a 90-day remote stint in Santiago, Chile starting 2026-06-15. Need to confirm impact on homebase, payroll withholding, benefits, and WFH stipend. Also wonder whether we can ship my company monitor there. TL;DR: what actions do I need to take? :airplane:

maria: Thanks Sam. Two quick Qs: will you keep your Redwood homebase as CA? Are you staying on US payroll (no secondment)? Are you still overlapping Redwood core hours?

sam: Keeping CA homebase, staying on US payroll, will maintain overlap with manager. No official secondment.

alex: From a tax standpoint, under 183-day rules this shouldn't create company nexus. Chile specifics look okay for 90 days but I'll run this by tax/legal to confirm. No guarantees until reviewed.

payroll-bot: Automated note — for temporary cross-border work under 183 days and with homebase unchanged, default payroll withholding remains US-based. See: https://redwood.example.com/hr/temp-remote-guidelines

jordan: Benefits note: our US medical plans generally cover emergency care abroad but not routine local care. Recommend short-term travel medical for Chile. For WFH stipend: we prorate by full months. For ~90 days you'd receive 3/12 of annual stipend.

sam: For the stipend, do I file an expense or is it automatic? And regarding equipment — I already have a company monitor on record; can it be shipped internationally?

maria: Stipend: submit via Expensify using the "WFH stipend - prorated" category and include the exact dates in the notes. Equipment: we can ship but need customs paperwork and the asset tag. You are responsible for import duties/taxes. Fill the equipment-shipping form: https://redwood.example.com/hr/equipment-shipping

jordan: Payroll team: might flag withholding but if you're on US payroll and no homebase change, nothing more is usually required. Keep travel docs and payslips in case you need to file locally. I'll notify payroll ops of the dates to prevent address/withholding drift.

alex: Legal: avoid client-facing activities, hiring, or contractor management in Chile without sign-off. Short-term IC/product work is fine, but those activities can trigger local registration obligations. I'll escalate to tax/legal and report back by EOD.

sam: Appreciate it. Any payroll documents I need to sign beforehand? Also can someone confirm emergency medical coverage while there?

maria: @lina from benefits can confirm emergency coverage. @jordan will follow on any payroll forms. Lina — can you confirm emergency coverage scope for Chile? :pray:

lina: Short answer: company medical plan covers emergency treatment globally for short trips. Non-emergency/routine care abroad is excluded. I'll DM recommended travel-insurance vendors and a short checklist (vaccines, meds, nearby clinics).

payroll-bot: Reminder — log a Temporary Address in Homebase (HRIS) at least 7 days before departure to toggle payroll/address flags.

sam: I'll submit the HRIS temporary address, expense request, and equipment shipping form this week. Thanks for the rapid help! :raised_hands:
